subject: Civil Engineering
title: Airport Pavements
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Airport Pavements.

hook.text: A Boeing 777 weighs 775,000 pounds at takeoff. The runway must handle that daily.

buildup.text: Airport pavements are 3-4 times thicker than highway pavements — massive loads demand it.

discovery.text: Taxiways need stronger pavement than runways — planes move slowly, concentrating load.

twist.text: Jet blast erodes pavement surfaces. Fuel spills dissolve asphalt binder.

climax.text: The FAA's PCN system rates every airport pavement for the maximum aircraft it can support.

punchline.text: Airport pavement carries the heaviest loads in all of civil engineering.

quiz.question: Why do taxiways need stronger pavement than runways?
options: Taxiways are used more frequently than runways
Planes move slowly on taxiways, concentrating their heavy loads in one spot longer
Taxiways are narrower, creating more stress per square foot

details.summary: Airport pavements must support aircraft weighing up to 500 tons with concentrated gear loads, withstand jet blast temperatures, and resist fuel spills. Runway and taxiway pavements are designed using aircraft classification numbers and pavement classification numbers that match pavement strength to.
details.whyItMatters: Airport pavement failure disrupts critical transportation infrastructure and creates safety hazards for aircraft. Design must balance extreme load requirements with the enormous costs of airfield construction.
takeaways: Aircraft tire pressures reach 1,500 kPa, far exceeding highway truck loads
Runway pavements can be 50 cm or more of concrete over engineered base layers
The ACN-PCN system matches aircraft weight ratings to pavement strength ratings

faq.question: How does airport pavement design differ from highway pavement design?
faq.answer: Airport pavements carry far heavier but less frequent loads, with tire pressures up to five times higher than trucks. Design uses specific aircraft gear configurations rather than standardized ESALs. Pavements must also resist jet fuel spills, jet blast heat, and de-icing chemical exposure.

faq.question: What is the ACN-PCN system used for airport pavements?
faq.answer: The Aircraft Classification Number represents the load demand an aircraft places on pavement based on its weight and gear configuration. The Pavement Classification Number represents the strength of the airfield pavement. An aircraft can operate on a pavement when its ACN does not exceed the PCN.
